title: A Molecular Gas Ring Hidden in the Sombrero Galaxy
question: What are the properties, distribution, and heating/excitation mechanisms of the molecular, atomic, and ionized gas and dust in the ring of M 104, and how do its [CII] and CO emissions compare to early-type and star-forming galaxies?

recipe.goal: Reduce and recalibrate Herschel/PACS [CII] unchopped spectroscopic data and VLT/MUSE optical cubes
recipe.method: Modified HIPE 15 unchopped pipeline with Python scripts to remove band-switch, long-term, and cosmic-ray transients and calibrate to the telescope background; reprocess 10 MUSE observations with MUSE pipeline 2.8.5 and shift velocity frame to LSRK.
key_parameters: PACS cube spatial pixel = 3 arcsec; MUSE cube spatial pixel = 0.4 arcsec; MUSE velocity shifts = -28.5 km/s (barycentric) and +0.9 km/s (LSRK)
assumptions: Telescope background is stable and dominates total flux over weak target flux

recipe.goal: Produce pixel-by-pixel line intensity, velocity, and velocity dispersion maps
recipe.method: Fit CO, [CII], and Halpha lines across the ALMA, PACS, and MUSE spectral cubes using sospex, masking pixels with SNR < 5.
Mask the central bulge and fit an ellipse to the infrared (IRAC Ch4, MIPS 24, PACS 70, 100, 160) and ALMA CO intensity images using direct linear least squares.
assumptions: The ring of M 104 is intrinsically circular

recipe.goal: Extract aperture spectra, fit emission/absorption lines, and analyze gas and stellar kinematics
recipe.method: Extract spectra in 59 apertures along the ring and interior (10.7'' circular diameter for PACS/MUSE; 14.3'' x 7.7'' elliptical beam shape for ALMA), fit CO and [CII] with sospex and optical spectra with showspectra, and fit linear v_los vs projected distance.
key_parameters: Circular aperture diameter = 10.7 arcsec; ALMA aperture = 14.3'' x 7.7'' ellipse
assumptions: Circular ring rotating with constant angular velocity Omega; distance = 31.1 Mpc (70 pc/arcsec)

recipe.goal: Classify regions into HII/Comp and LIER using optical emission line diagnostics
recipe.method: Construct BPT and weak-line diagnostic diagrams ([NII]/Halpha vs [OIII]/Halpha and EW(Halpha) vs [NII]/Halpha) from MUSE aperture line fluxes to classify regions.
key_parameters: 3-sigma lower limits used when Hbeta is barely visible

recipe.goal: Smooth multi-wavelength photometry and fit SEDs to derive FIR luminosity, attenuated UV, SFR, and PAH fluxes
recipe.method: Smooth FUV to PACS 160 um images to 10.7'' resolution, extract fluxes in the 10.7'' circular apertures, fit SEDs with CIGALE, integrate models for FIR (8-1000 um) and attenuated UV (91.2-206.6 nm), and subtract non-PAH continuum from IRAC4 and WISE3 to get 7.7 and 11.3 um PAH fluxes.
key_parameters: Common resolution = 10.7''; FIR integration range = 8-1000 um; UV_att integration range = 91.2-206.6 nm; f_AGN = 0 for ring regions, f_AGN = 0.1, 0.25, 0.5 for interior regions; Z = Z_odot
assumptions: Energy balance between UV absorption and IR emission; Bruzual & Charlot (2003) SSP with Chabrier (2003) IMF; Calzetti (2000) attenuation; Draine et al. (2014) dust models; Fritz et al. (2006) AGN model; 10% uncertainty on CIGALE-derived quantities.

recipe.goal: Estimate total and resolved molecular hydrogen (H2) masses and compare with SFR (Kennicutt-Schmidt relation)
recipe.method: Integrate total and aperture CO(1-0) emission, apply a factor of 2 optical depth correction and Eq. 3 of Bolatto et al. (2013) to obtain M(H2), and divide M(H2) and CIGALE SFR by deprojected aperture area.
key_parameters: Optical depth correction factor = 2; inclination = 84.3 deg; distance = 31.1 Mpc
assumptions: CO(1-0) optical depth correction of 2 (cite: Hughes2017) and CO-to-H2 conversion from Eq. 3 of (cite: Bolatto2013)

answer_key.quantity: Molecular hydrogen mass of the ring of M 104

evidence.quote: From the total intensity of the CO line we estimate a molecular hydrogen mass of $0.9\times10^{9}$M$_\odot$, a value intermediate between those of early type galaxies and the content of the molecular ring of our galaxy.
By applying the conversion from Eq. 3 from (cite: Bolatto2013), we find out that the total molecular hydrogen mass of the ring of M 104 is $0.9\times10^9$ M$_\odot$.
| Inclination | 84.3$^o\pm0.2^o$ | This work |
Since the images which are less disturbed by the nuclear emission are the PACS 160$\mu$m and the ALMA CO intensity image, we accept the value fitted in the case of the CO: 84.3$^o\pm0.2^o$.
| v$_{sys}$ | 1089.2$\pm$1.1 km/s | [LSRK] This work |
The systemic velocity from the optical emission line is $(1089.1\pm1.8)$ km/s, while the one based on CO data is $(1089.2\pm1.1)$ km/s.

answer_key.quantity: Systemic velocity v_sys (from optical emission lines)

evidence.quote: The systemic velocity from the optical emission line is $(1089.1\pm1.8)$ km/s, while the one based on CO data is $(1089.2\pm1.1)$ km/s.

answer_key.quantity: Angular velocity of galaxy rotation Omega (from ALMA CO)

evidence.quote: The absolute values of the angular velocity for the CO data and the optical emission lines, which have the smallest errors, are $(35.0\pm0.1)$ km s$^{-1}$kpc$^{-1}$ and $(35.2\pm0.2)$ km s$^{-1}$kpc$^{-1}$, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Angular velocity of galaxy rotation Omega (from optical emission lines)

evidence.quote: The absolute values of the angular velocity for the CO data and the optical emission lines, which have the smallest errors, are $(35.0\pm0.1)$ km s$^{-1}$kpc$^{-1}$ and $(35.2\pm0.2)$ km s$^{-1}$kpc$^{-1}$, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: CO/FIR ratio range in M 104 ring

evidence.quote: It is also notable that while the CO/FIR values from NGC 7331 are distributed over a range of $3.9\times10^{-6} - 6.7\times10^{-5}$, M 104 only covers a range of $1.4\times10^{-6} - 5.6\times10^{-6}$, which is both lower and much more constrained than NGC 7331.

While the regions from the three star–forming galaxies are fairly evenly distributed from $\sim 0-4$, regions from M 104 all fall between 0.5 and 2.2, implying a much more uniform population of PAHs across the disk.

score_reason: The ALMA analysis uses standard archival cubes as-is, all 59 aperture coordinates and extracted fluxes are tabulated in Appendix B (Table 6), CIGALE grid parameters are fully specified in Table 5, and the spectral fitting tools (sospex, showspectra) are public on GitHub. Minor deductions for unreleased custom PACS transient Python scripts and unstated exact alpha_CO value and global CO integration mask.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA dataset (2018.1.00034.S) is public and used directly as an archival product without custom re-imaging, aperture coordinates and CO fluxes are explicitly tabulated for verification, and the main ALMA-derived results (inclination = 84.3 deg, v_sys = 1089.2 km/s, Omega = 35.0 km/s/kpc, M_H2 = 0.9e9 M_odot, and aperture CO fluxes) are clear numeric targets.
